# Commands and results

`scripts/coverage-gate.ps1` passed: 55 protobuf types, 131 field fixtures, 55 explicit-zero fixtures, 6 corrupt frames, 19 categories, 11 developer frames, 10 client responses, 26 incoming frames; default and Frida-tagged statement coverage were both 100.0%, and unit, race and vet exited 0. `scripts/build-windows.ps1` exited 0. The live matrix established the 9421 upstream and exercised all seven required domains, but `scripts/smoke-windows.ps1` then used `Stop-Process -Force`; the user observed that opening the miniapp immediately ended in a flash-close. The live lifecycle verification therefore failed.

# Skipped checks

Graceful Windows process-group shutdown has not yet been implemented or live-verified. All automated receipts must be regenerated after the fix because the current revision binding is stale.

# Spec consistency

The protocol and simulated CDP scope remains consistent with the specification. The Windows smoke harness is inconsistent with the graceful shutdown requirement because it force-terminates the bridge process and bypasses Agent unload, Frida detach and application listener shutdown.

# Known limitations and risks

The observed flash-close is a release blocker. Current evidence does not yet distinguish target reaction to abrupt upstream loss from another detach-path defect, so the next Build iteration must use a process group, deliver `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`, require a zero exit, verify port release, and record whether the target miniapp remains open.

# Conclusion

Fail. Return to Build to replace forced smoke termination with graceful Windows shutdown, add tests, rebuild, rerun coverage, and repeat live validation with the target miniapp remaining open after bridge shutdown.
